title: Weighted Dip
summary: Parallel-bar dip with added load: chest and triceps 0.8, front delts 0.5. A bodyweight press with a long stretch.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: dip bars or power tower; dip belt; weight plates or dumbbells or kettlebells.

muscles.why: The lower chest pulls the arm down and forward; mid/lower 0.8, upper 0.32.
The triceps lock out; short heads 0.8, long head 0.4.
The front delts help from the stretched position at the bottom.

setup.text: Belt with plate or dumbbell between the legs.
Start at the top, arms locked.

form_cues.why: Lowering until the upper arms are about parallel to the floor.

form_cues.cue: Lower until shoulders are just below elbows
Stay upright for more triceps, lean for more chest

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Swinging the legs to kick the weight up.
mistakes.fix: Start with bodyweight dips for clean reps, then add load.

misconceptions.myth: Every set has to go to failure to grow.
misconceptions.reality: Stopping a few reps short gave similar growth to failure in a meta-analysis; growth tends to rise as sets get closer to failure, but the exact curve is uncertain.

lower_risk.text: When you add load, the app suggests one bodyweight-only set of 5 first (assisted machines: one set with one step more assistance). Without added load the first working set is its own warm-up.
The app counts your effective load (bodyweight share plus added load) and suggests more weight only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range.
Aim for about 3 reps in reserve in the 6-10 rep range. Stop a rep or two short; the bottom is hard to get out of when tired.
Use the depth you can control; don't drop into the bottom.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Decline barbell bench: the same lower-chest bias with more load.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only
alternatives.why: Push-ups: grew the pecs similarly to light bench when taken hard.

notes: Dips have not been compared with other presses for growth in a study the app cites.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
